purpose: Reproducible benchmark for TIE compliance evaluation. Used in P2.3 experiments.
provenance: Synthetic — all organizations, URLs, and data are fictional. Created by TrustForge research team.
ground_truth_methodology: Rule-based derivation from DPDP Act 2023 statutory text and TrustForge control definitions. Labels are NOT derived from TIE model outputs. Labels represent independently reasoned expected outcomes based on the evidence profile.
disclaimer: These labels represent rule-justified expected outcomes for benchmark purposes. They are NOT authoritative legal determinations. Do not present them as expert-reviewed compliance certifications.

organizations.name: Synthetic Org A — Strong Privacy Practice
organizations.scenario: Well-documented organization with comprehensive privacy infrastructure: public privacy notice, HTTPS+HSTS, consent banner with withdrawal, DPO published, processor contracts documented, breach plan in place, defined retention, automated erasure, rights portal operational.

wizard_answers.retention: 12 months post account closure, then deleted

TF-PRIV-001.justification: Privacy policy publicly linked — direct Section 5 requirement met

TF-PRIV-002.justification: English + Hindi available — Section 5 Eighth Schedule requirement met

TF-PRIV-003.justification: Consent banner present — Section 6 free/specific/informed consent indicator present

TF-PRIV-004.justification: Consent banner present — withdrawal mechanism to be evaluated by TIE

TF-PRIV-005.justification: Purposes documented with lawful basis (consent/service delivery) — Section 4

TF-SEC-001.justification: HTTPS + HSTS both detected — deterministic PASS

TF-SEC-002.justification: CSP + XCTO + Referrer-Policy all detected — deterministic PASS

TF-SEC-004.justification: No third-party trackers detected + consent banner present — no pre-consent loading

TF-TRANS-001.justification: Grievance officer named and contact published — Section 8(6)

TF-TRANS-002.justification: Privacy policy present + data categories documented — Section 5(a)

TF-GOV-001.justification: Processors listed with contracts mentioned — Section 8(7)

TF-LIFE-002.justification: Automated erasure process in place — Section 12(d)

TF-LIFE-003.justification: Limited data collection aligned with stated purposes — Section 4

TF-RIGHTS-001.justification: Access right documented and mechanism present — Section 11

TF-RIGHTS-002.justification: Correction and erasure rights documented — Section 12

TF-RIGHTS-004.justification: Rights process documented in privacy notice — Section 5(b)

organizations.name: Synthetic Org B — Missing Privacy Notice
organizations.scenario: Organization operates a website with HTTPS but has no privacy policy link. No consent banner. Tracker scripts load on page load.

TF-PRIV-001.justification: No privacy policy link detected — direct Section 5 violation

TF-PRIV-002.justification: No notice exists so language availability cannot be assessed

TF-PRIV-003.justification: No consent banner detected — Section 6 consent mechanism absent

TF-PRIV-004.justification: No consent mechanism means withdrawal ease cannot be evaluated — Section 6

TF-PRIV-005.justification: Service delivery is a legitimate basis but no documented lawful basis framework — Section 4

TF-SEC-001.justification: HTTPS detected but HSTS absent — deterministic POTENTIAL_GAP

TF-SEC-002.justification: No security headers detected — deterministic POTENTIAL_GAP

TF-SEC-003.justification: No breach plan — Section 8(4) readiness absent

TF-SEC-004.justification: Third-party trackers detected before consent — no lawful basis for processing — Section 4

TF-TRANS-002.justification: No privacy notice — data categories cannot be disclosed — Section 5(a)

TF-GOV-001.justification: No processors documented — no processor contracts — Section 8(7)

TF-GOV-002.justification: No rights mechanism documented — accuracy practices unknown

TF-LIFE-003.justification: Purposes listed but no minimisation framework documented — Section 4

TF-RIGHTS-001.justification: No rights documented — access right unavailable — Section 11

TF-RIGHTS-002.justification: No rights documented — correction/erasure unavailable — Section 12

organizations.name: Synthetic Org C — Inadequate Consent (Pre-ticked)
organizations.scenario: Organization has privacy policy and HTTPS but uses pre-ticked consent checkboxes. No clear withdrawal mechanism.
organizations.scenario_notes: consent_banner=true detected by scanner but wizard reveals it uses pre-ticked checkboxes — invalid consent under Section 6

TF-PRIV-002.justification: Only English mentioned — Eighth Schedule compliance not confirmed

TF-PRIV-003.justification: Pre-ticked boxes do not constitute 'clear affirmative action' — Section 6 invalid consent

TF-PRIV-005.justification: Marketing purpose requires consent; pre-ticked boxes invalid — Section 4/6

TF-SEC-002.justification: CSP and Referrer-Policy absent — deterministic POTENTIAL_GAP

TF-SEC-004.justification: Trackers detected with invalid consent — no lawful basis — Section 4

TF-GOV-001.justification: One processor listed but no contract status documented — Section 8(7)

TF-GOV-002.justification: Access right documented but accuracy practices unclear — Section 8(1)

TF-LIFE-001.justification: 5-year retention mentioned but necessity not demonstrated — Section 8(5)

TF-LIFE-003.justification: Marketing collects purchase history — proportionality questionable — Section 4

TF-RIGHTS-002.justification: Access mentioned but correction/erasure not documented — Section 12

TF-RIGHTS-003.justification: Grievance officer named and contact published — Section 13

organizations.name: Synthetic Org D — Weak Transport Security
organizations.scenario: Organization operates over HTTP only. No HTTPS. Has privacy policy and consent. Security headers all absent.

TF-PRIV-004.justification: Withdrawal ease not documented in wizard

TF-PRIV-005.justification: Newsletter with consent — lawful basis present — Section 4

TF-SEC-001.justification: No HTTPS detected — deterministic FAIL — Section 8(3) safeguard absent

TF-GOV-001.justification: No processors engaged — Section 8(7) does not apply

TF-GOV-002.justification: Correction documented — reasonable accuracy practices — Section 8(1)

TF-LIFE-003.justification: Email only for newsletter — minimised — Section 4

TF-RIGHTS-004.justification: Rights process in privacy notice — Section 5(b)

TF-PRIV-004.justification: Withdrawal mechanism not specified in wizard

TF-PRIV-005.justification: E-commerce = service delivery = lawful basis present — Section 4

TF-SEC-002.justification: All security headers present — deterministic PASS

TF-SEC-004.justification: No trackers, consent banner present — Section 4

TF-GOV-001.justification: Processors listed but no contract status provided — Section 8(7)

TF-GOV-002.justification: E-commerce requires accurate billing data — practices inferred — Section 8(1)

TF-LIFE-001.justification: 7-year billing (likely legal requirement), 2-year for others — Section 8(5)

TF-LIFE-003.justification: Data collected aligns with e-commerce purposes — Section 4

TF-RIGHTS-004.justification: Rights documented in privacy notice — Section 5(b)

organizations.name: Synthetic Org F — Weak Retention/Erasure
organizations.scenario: Organization has no defined retention limits. Data retained 'indefinitely' or 'as long as needed'. No automated erasure.

TF-PRIV-005.justification: Product improvement purpose — consent needed, assess banner quality — Section 4

TF-SEC-002.justification: Missing CSP, XCTO, Referrer — deterministic POTENTIAL_GAP

TF-TRANS-001.justification: Grievance officer and contact published — Section 8(6)

TF-GOV-002.justification: Only access right documented — accuracy practices unclear

TF-LIFE-001.justification: Indefinite retention explicitly stated — violates Section 8(5) necessity principle

TF-LIFE-002.justification: erasure_automated=false, indefinite retention — Section 12(d) not met

TF-LIFE-003.justification: Usage logs for product improvement — proportionality needs review — Section 4
